NASD RULE 3030: JONES FAILED TO DISCLOSE HIS OUTSIDE BUSINESS ACTIVITIES TO A MEMBER FIRM. JONES WAS A REGISTERED REPRESENTATIVE AND PRINCIPAL OF A MEMBER FIRM AND THE FIRM WAS BOTH A FINRA BROKER-DEALER AND AN INTRODUCING COMMODITIES BROKER WITH THE NATIONAL FUTURES ASSOCIATION (NFA), AND JONES CONDUCTED SECURITIES BUSINESS AND COMMODITIES BUSINESS THROUGH THE FIRM. BECAUSE OF THAT FIRM'S DUAL MEMBERSHIPS, JONES' COMMODITIES BUSINESS DID NOT CONSTITUTE AN OUTSIDE BUSINESS ACTIVITY WHILE HE WAS ASSOCIATED WITH THE FIRM. THE FIRM CEASED OPERATIONS, BY THAT TIME JONES HAD MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO MOVE HIS SECURITIES BUSINESS ELSEWHERE, AND JONES BECAME A REGISTERED REPRESENTATIVE OF ANOTHER MEMBER FIRM. THE FIRM DID NOT HAVE A COMMODITIES-BROKERAGE BUSINESS. THUS, JONES AND ANOTHER FORMER REPRESENTATIVE OF HIS PREVIOUS FIRM ESTABLISHED A CORPORATION. THE CORPORATION ALSO BECAME AN INTRODUCING COMMODITIES BROKER WITH THE NFA. JONES HAS BEEN AN OFFICER AND DIRECTOR OF THE CORPORATION SINCE ITS INCORPORATION, AND HAS BEEN COMPENSATED BY THE CORPORATION AS AN INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. JONES DID NOT IMMEDIATELY DISCLOSE HIS INVOLVEMENT WITH THE CORPORATION TO HIS PRESENT FIRM. JONES COMPLETED A REPRESENTATIVE QUESTIONNAIRE OF THE FIRM AND FAILED TO CORRECTLY DISCLOSE HIS ENGAGEMENT WITH THE OUTSIDE BUSINESS. AT THAT TIME, HOWEVER, JONES WAS A DIRECTOR AND OFFICER OF THE CORPORATION, WHICH WAS UNRELATED TO THE FIRM. JONES COMPLETED ANOTHER REPRESENTATIVE QUESTIONNAIRE, AND HE ANSWERED THE OUTSIDE BUSINESS ACTIVITY QUESTION CORRECTLY BY IDENTIFYING HIS INVOLVEMENT WITH THE CORPORATION. JONES SUBSEQUENTLY PROVIDED THE FIRM WITH ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE CORPORATION.
